The '''2018–19 La Liga''' season, also known as '''LaLiga [[Banco Santander|Santander]]''' for sponsorship reasons,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.laliga.es/en/news/laliga-and-santander-strike-title-sponsorship-deal |title=LaLiga and Santander strike title sponsorship deal |date=21 July 2016 |publisher=La Liga |access-date=21 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160725161336/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/laliga-and-santander-strike-title-sponsorship-deal |archive-date=25 July 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was the 88th since its establishment. The season began on 17 August 2018 and concluded on 19 May 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.laliga.es/en/calendar-time |title=Competition calendar |publisher=La Liga |access-date=27 July 2018}}</ref> Fixtures for the 2018–19 season were announced on 24 July 2018.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.laliga.es/en/news/the-fixtures-for-laliga-santander-201819 |title=The fixtures for LaLiga Santander 2018/19 |date=24 July 2018 |publisher=La Liga |access-date=27 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724154033/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/the-fixtures-for-laliga-santander-201819 |archive-date=24 July 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> This was the first La Liga season to use the [[Video assistant referee|VAR]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11827/11272929/la-liga-confirms-video-assistant-referee-var-will-be-used-from-next-season |title=La Liga confirms Video Assistant Referee (VAR) will be used from next season |last=Charles |first=Andy |date=2 March 2018 |work=Sky Sports |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref>

[[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] were the defending champions, and they secured a second consecutive title with three games to spare following victory over [[Levante UD|Levante]] on 27 April.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/apr/29/barcelona-make-the-extraordinary-seem-normal-to-wrap-up-another-title-lionel-messi
|title =Barcelona make the extraordinary seem normal to wrap up another title|date=29 April 2019|work=The Guardian|access-date=30 April 2019}}</ref> [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], [[Rayo Vallecano]] and [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2017–18 Segunda División]]. They replaced [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] and [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]], who were relegated to the [[2018–19 Segunda División]].

This is the first season since [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09]] that did not feature the league's all time [[List of La Liga top scorers|second-highest scorer]] [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], who departed to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the summer.

==Summary==
Several clubs made managerial changes before the start of the season. Among them were [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], when [[Zinedine Zidane]] resigned following the club's third consecutive [[UEFA Champions League]] victory. He was replaced by [[Julen Lopetegui]], who was managing the Spain national team at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia at the time of announcement and was dismissed from that job as a result.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lowe |first1=Sid |title=Spain sack manager Julen Lopetegui as Fernando Hierro takes over |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/13/julen-lopetegui-sacked-spain-manager-real-madrid-job |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=The Guardian |date=13 June 2018}}</ref> Other incomers included [[Pablo Machín]] at [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], who was hired after his success with newly promoted [[Girona FC|Girona]] the previous season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sevilla appoint Pablo Machin as new manager after Girona success |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11834/11388498/sevilla-appoint-pablo-machin-as-new-manager-after-girona-success |access-date=2 October 2018 |publisher=Sky Sports |date=28 May 2018}}</ref>

In the transfer window, the biggest deal saw Real Madrid lose [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] for a fee of €112 million; the Portuguese forward had scored 450 goals in 438 games during his nine years in the Spanish capital.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cristiano Ronaldo: Juventus sign Real Madrid forward for £99.2m |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44785173 |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=BBC Sport |date=10 July 2018}}</ref> Real Madrid's additions included Belgium international goalkeeper [[Thibaut Courtois]] for €35 million from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], and striker [[Mariano Díaz|Mariano]] returned to the club from [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] for €22 million.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea confirm €35m Courtois sale to Real Madrid as Kovacic moves to London |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/chelsea-confirm-35m-courtois-sale-to-real-madrid-as-kovacic/hyr6yvpt6fza1wm8ydfeogxtv |access-date=2 October 2018 |publisher=Goal.com |date=8 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Cerezo |first1=Hugo |title=Official: Mariano Diaz returns to Real |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/08/29/5b85a89d468aeb33298b45df.html |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=Marca|location=Spain|date=29 August 2018}}</ref> Defending champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] added [[Clément Lenglet]] to their defence, [[Arturo Vidal]] to midfield, and spent over €40 million on Brazilian forward [[Malcom (footballer)|Malcom]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rojo |first1=Luis F. |title=Mixed displays from Barcelona's new signings |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2018/08/13/5b716ca5ca4741cc098b45bf.html |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=Marca|location=Spain|date=13 August 2018}}</ref> Players exiting Barcelona included [[Andrés Iniesta]] at the end of a successful 16-year-spell, as he signed for [[Vissel Kobe]] in Japan.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McKirdy |first1=Andrew |title=Vissel sign ex-Barcelona star Andres Iniesta to massive deal |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2018/05/24/soccer/j-league/vissel-sign-ex-barcelona-star-andres-iniesta-massive-deal/ |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=The Japan Times |date=24 May 2018}}</ref>

Veterans [[Gabi (footballer, born 1983)|Gabi]] and [[Fernando Torres]] also left [[Atlético Madrid]] for new teams in Asia,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Barbero |first1=Alberto R. |title=Atletico remember the contributions of Gabi and Fernando Torres |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/08/17/5b76d793ca47415f5f8b4610.html |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=Marca|location=Spain|date=17 August 2018}}</ref> while the same club welcomed in the likes of [[2018 FIFA World Cup|World Cup-winning]] French midfielder [[Thomas Lemar]] and Portugal's [[Gelson Martins]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Atletico Madrid sign Gelson Martins on free transfer after Sporting exit |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/gelson-martins-atletico-madrid-transfer-news-sporting-thomas-lemar-a8463206.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/gelson-martins-atletico-madrid-transfer-news-sporting-thomas-lemar-a8463206.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=The Independent |date=25 July 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref> After a successful previous season, in which the team finished fourth and returned to the Champions League, [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] made permanent the loan signing of Portuguese winger [[Gonçalo Guedes]] from [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] and [[Geoffrey Kondogbia]] from [[Inter Milan]]. Forward [[Simone Zaza]] and midfielder [[João Cancelo]] both left to Italy, while [[Kevin Gameiro]] arrived as replacement.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United v Valencia facts |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0249-0e9916deab7e-41df17896438-1000--manchester-united-v-valencia-facts/ |access-date=2 October 2018 |publisher=UEFA |date=25 September 2018}}</ref> [[Athletic Bilbao]] sold [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] to Chelsea for €80 million, a world record fee for a goalkeeper.<ref>{{cite news |title=Soccer - Chelsea sign Spanish goalkeeper Kepa for world record fee |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-che-kepa/soccer-bilbaos-kepa-pays-80-million-euro-release-fee-ahead-of-record-chelsea-move-idUKKBN1KT197 |access-date=2 October 2018 |work=Reuters |date=8 August 2018}}</ref>

The tenth round of matches featured the first ''[[El Clásico]]'' of the season, which Barcelona won 5–1 at home against Real Madrid with a [[hat-trick]] by [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]]. The result put Madrid into 9th place,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jennings |first1=Patrick |title=Barcelona 5&ndash;1 Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45995215 |access-date=28 October 2018 |work=BBC Sport |date=28 October 2018}}</ref> and led to the dismissal of Lopetegui after only five months.<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid sack Julen Lopetegui as manager |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45935137 |access-date=30 October 2018 |work=BBC Sport |date=29 October 2018}}</ref> Other early pace-setters included Sevilla with their prolific strike partnership of [[André Silva (footballer, born 1995)|André Silva]] and [[Wissam Ben Yedder]],<ref>{{cite news |title=PSG have not forgotten about Sevilla's Wissam Ben Yedder |url=https://www.sport-english.com/en/news/futbol-internacional/psg-have-not-forgotten-about-sevillas-wissam-ben-yedder-7106245 |access-date=28 October 2018 |work=Sport |date=23 October 2018}}</ref> [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] who were briefly league leaders in mid-October,<ref>{{cite news |last1=García |first1=Óscar |title=Surprise package Alaves are provisional LaLiga Santander leaders after Celta win |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/cronica/2018/10/19/5bca4b71e2704eed658b459e.html |access-date=28 October 2018 |work=Marca|location=Spain|date=19 October 2018}}</ref> [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], and [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] who had been taken over by former Brazil international [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Espanyol concede late to Valladolid, lose chance to take La Liga lead |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report?gameId=521823 |access-date=28 October 2018 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |date=27 October 2018}}</ref>

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of 20 teams will contest the league, including 17 sides from the [[2017–18 La Liga|2017–18 season]] and three promoted from the [[2017–18 Segunda División]]. This will include the two top teams from the Segunda División, and the winners of the [[2018 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]].
 
;Teams relegated to Segunda División
 
The first team to be relegated from [[La Liga]] were [[Málaga CF|Málaga]]. Their relegation was ensured on 19 April 2018, following a late 0−1 defeat to [[Levante UD|Levante]], ending their 10-year spell in the top division.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/us/news/malaga-relegated-laliga-after-late-defeat|title=Malaga relegated from LaLiga after late defeat|work=Four Four Two|date=19 April 2018|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref>
 
The second team to be relegated were [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], after a 0−4 home defeat to [[Deportivo Alavés]] on 22 April 2018, ending their three-year spell in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/las-palmas/story/3467949/las-palmas-relegated-in-la-liga-after-4-0-loss-to-alaves|title=Las Palmas relegated in La Liga after 4-0 loss to Alaves|agency=Associated Press|publisher=ESPN|date=22 April 2018|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref>
 
The last team to be relegated were [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]], following a 2−4 home loss to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on 29 April 2018. This result ensured Deportivo's third relegation in seven years, and also handed Barcelona their 25th La Liga title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/04/30/football/1525094263_093828.html|title=Deportivo relegated from LaLiga for third time in seven years|first=Luis|last=de la Cruz|work=AS English|date=30 April 2018|access-date=30 April 2018|archive-date=1 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501095402/https://en.as.com/en/2018/04/30/football/1525094263_093828.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
 
;Teams promoted from Segunda División
 
On 21 May 2018, [[SD Huesca|Huesca]] were promoted to La Liga for the first time ever by winning 2–0 at [[CD Lugo|Lugo]].
 
[[Rayo Vallecano]] was the second team to earn promotion to La Liga on 27 May 2018 by winning against Lugo as well, this time 1–0. Rayo returned after a two-year absence.
 
[[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] was the last team to be promoted after beating [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]] and [[CD Numancia|Numancia]] in the play-offs. Valladolid returned to top division after 4 years.
 
This was the first season since the [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15 season]] without any teams from the [[archipelago]]s of Spain (teams located on the [[Balearic Islands]] and [[Canary Islands]]) since [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] was relegated and [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] failed to qualify for the [[2018 Segunda División play-offs|promotion play-offs]].

===Matches outside Spain===
On 16 August 2018, La Liga signed a 15-year agreement with Relevant Sports (owners of the [[International Champions Cup]]) to schedule one match per season within the United States. This would mark the first time ever that an official La Liga league match would be held there.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Draper |first1=Kevin |title=La Liga Will Bring Regular-Season Matches to America |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/16/sports/soccer/la-liga-united-states.html |access-date=18 August 2018 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Carlisle |first1=Jeff |title=La Liga set to play first game in United States in new marketing deal |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/spanish-primera-division/story/3599220/la-liga-set-to-play-first-game-in-united-states--in-new-marketing-deal |access-date=18 August 2018 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=16 August 2018}}</ref> The match between [[Girona FC|Girona]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], to be played on 27 January 2019, was selected to be played in [[Miami]], but it required the approval of the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/spanish-primera-division/story/3629136/la-liga-formally-propose-girona-barcelona-game-to-be-played-in-us|publisher=ESPN|access-date=17 September 2018|date=10 September 2018|title=La Liga formally propose Girona-Barcelona game to be played in U.S.}}</ref> On 21 September 2018, the Spanish Football Federation denied approval of the match being held in Miami.<ref>{{cite news|last=Moñino|first=Ladislao Javier|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2018/09/21/actualidad/1537524880_151620.html|title=La Federación comunica a LaLiga que no autoriza el Girona-Barcelona en Miami|language=es|trans-title=The Federation notifies LaLiga that they do not authorize the Girona-Barcelona match in Miami|date=21 September 2018|access-date=21 September 2018|newspaper=[[El País]]}}</ref> On 26 October 2018, following a request for guidance from the Spanish Football Federation, [[US Soccer]] and [[CONCACAF]], the [[FIFA Council]] discussed La Liga's proposal. At the end of the meeting, the FIFA Council stated that "Consistent with the opinion expressed by the Football Stakeholders Committee, the Council emphasised the sporting principle that official league matches must be played within the territory of the respective member association".<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=FIFA Council makes key decisions for the future of football development |url=https://www.fifa.com/about-fifa/news/y=2018/m=10/news=fifa-council-makes-key-decisions-for-the-future-of-football-development.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181026182831/https://www.fifa.com/about-fifa/news/y=2018/m=10/news=fifa-council-makes-key-decisions-for-the-future-of-football-development.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 October 2018 |date=26 October 2018 |access-date=29 October 2018 }}</ref> On 13 December 2018, Barcelona left their disposition to play the match in Miami without effect.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2018/12/10/actualidad/1544470637_490934.html|title=El Barcelona deja 'sin efecto' su disposición a jugar en Miami|language=es|trans-title=Barcelona leaves "without effect" their disposition to play in Miami|date=12 December 2018|access-date=12 December 2018|newspaper=[[El País]]}}</ref>

===Zamora Trophy===
{{ multiple image
 | align = right
 | direction = upright
 | image1 = Jan Oblak 2017.jpg
 | width1 = 120
 | footer = [[Jan Oblak]] won his fourth consecutive Zamora Trophy, the first player to do so since [[Víctor Valdés]] from 2009 to 2012.}}

The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref name="zamora">{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/primera-division/zamora.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=21 February 2023 |location=Spain}}</ref>
